title: Contains Duplicate
twist: Warm-up: one set remembers every number you have seen.
prompt: Does any number show up more than once in this array?
signal: You keep asking “have I seen this before?”, so keep a set.

title: Valid Anagram
twist: Warm-up: count the letters here, count them there, compare.
prompt: Do two strings use exactly the same letters, the same number of times?
signal: Only the letter counts matter, so count and compare.

title: Two Sum
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Find the two numbers in an unsorted array that add up to a target.
signal: Each number tells you exactly which partner it needs, so look the partner up.

title: Group Anagrams
twist: Same letter counts, now used as a key for each group.
prompt: Sort a list of words into buckets, so words made of the same letters land together.
signal: Words that belong together share a key: their sorted letters or letter counts.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
twist: Count everything first, then keep the k biggest counts.
prompt: Return the k values that appear most often in an array.
signal: Count with a map, then bucket values by their count.

title: Encode and Decode Strings
twist: Store each length up front, so decoding never guesses.
prompt: Squeeze a list of strings into one string and get them back, whatever characters they hold.
signal: Write each length first, so you never need a separator that could clash.

title: Product of Array Except Self
twist: Prefix and suffix products, with no division allowed.
prompt: For each position, give the product of all the other numbers, without division.
signal: Everything to my left times everything to my right: two running products.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
twist: A set finds each run’s start in constant time.
prompt: Find the longest run of neighbouring values, like 4, 5, 6, in an unsorted array, in linear time.
signal: A set lets you count only from the true start of each run.

title: Valid Palindrome
twist: Warm-up: ends walk inward, skipping anything that isn’t a letter or digit.
prompt: Does this sentence read the same both ways once you ignore case and punctuation?
signal: Compare the outside pair, then work inward.

title: 3Sum
twist: Sort first, then run two pointers from every start.
prompt: Find every unique trio of numbers that adds up to zero.
signal: Sort, fix one number, then close in on the other two from both ends.

title: Container With Most Water
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Pick two vertical lines that hold the most water between them.
signal: Start with the widest pair. Only moving the shorter line can ever help.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
twist: Warm-up: the cheapest price so far is your window’s left edge.
prompt: Given daily prices, find the biggest profit from one buy followed by one sell.
signal: Hold the cheapest day so far on the left and let the right edge scan.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: How long is the longest unbroken stretch of a string with no repeated letter?
signal: An unbroken stretch with a rule: grow on the right, shrink on the left when it breaks.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
twist: Same window, but shrink only when replacements run out.
prompt: You may change up to k letters. How long a run of one letter can you make?
signal: A stretch is fine while its length minus its most common letter is at most k.

title: Minimum Window Substring
twist: Grow until the window is valid, then shrink it as small as it goes.
prompt: Find the shortest piece of a string that contains every letter of another string.
signal: Grow until it covers everything, then shrink while it still does.

title: Valid Parentheses
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Check that every bracket in a string closes in the right order.
signal: The newest open bracket must close first: last in, first out.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: A sorted array was rotated at an unknown point. Find its smallest value in log time.
signal: Comparing the middle to the right end tells you which half holds the drop.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
twist: Same halving, but first ask which half is sorted.
prompt: Find a target in a sorted array that was rotated at an unknown point, in log time.
signal: One half is always in order. Check whether the target sits inside it.

title: Reverse Linked List
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Flip a chain of nodes so the last one comes first.
signal: Repoint one arrow at a time, holding on to the rest of the chain.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
twist: Warm-up: walk both lists, always taking the smaller head.
prompt: Combine two sorted chains of nodes into one sorted chain.
signal: Compare the two heads and relink the smaller one.

title: Linked List Cycle
twist: A fast pointer laps a slow one exactly when a loop exists.
prompt: Does this chain of nodes loop back on itself?
signal: A fast walker and a slow walker only meet if there’s a loop.

title: Reorder List
twist: Find the middle, reverse the back half, then weave.
prompt: Rearrange a chain as first, last, second, second-last, and so on.
signal: Find the middle, reverse the back half, then weave the two.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
twist: Two pointers, n apart, walk to the end together.
prompt: Delete the node n places from the end of a chain, in one pass.
signal: Two walkers n apart: when the front one hits the end, the back one is in place.

title: Merge K Sorted Lists
twist: Merge pairs again and again until one list is left.
prompt: Combine k sorted chains of nodes into one sorted chain.
signal: Merge in pairs, halving the number of lists each round.

title: Invert Binary Tree
twist: Warm-up: swap each node’s children, top down.
prompt: Mirror a tree so every left child swaps with its right child.
signal: Handle one node and let recursion do the rest.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: How many levels does this tree have at its deepest point?
signal: My depth is one more than my deepest child.

title: Same Tree
twist: Walk both trees together; every pair must match.
prompt: Do these two tree shapes hold the same values in the same places?
signal: Walk both at once. One mismatch ends it.

title: Subtree of Another Tree
twist: Same-tree check, tried at every node.
prompt: Does a smaller tree appear exactly inside a bigger one?
signal: Run the same-tree check from every node.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
twist: Split point where the targets part ways.
prompt: Find the lowest shared parent of two values, in a tree where left is smaller and right is bigger.
signal: Walk down until the two values fall on different sides.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
twist: A queue walks the tree one level at a time.
prompt: List a tree’s values row by row, from the top down.
signal: A queue hands you each level in turn.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
twist: Each node inherits a valid range from above.
prompt: Check that everything left of a node is smaller and everything right of it is bigger, at every node.
signal: Pass an allowed range down as you go.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
twist: In-order walk, counting until you reach k.
prompt: Find the kth smallest value in a tree where left is smaller and right is bigger.
signal: An in-order walk visits values in sorted order.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
twist: The preorder head splits the inorder list.
prompt: Rebuild a tree from its preorder and inorder listings.
signal: Preorder names the root. Inorder splits left from right.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
twist: Like depth, but the best path may bend.
prompt: Find the path between any two nodes with the largest total.
signal: Each node passes up its best straight arm and scores its best bend.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
twist: Level order out, level order back in.
prompt: Turn a tree into a string and rebuild the exact same tree from it.
signal: Walk it and write down the gaps too.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Build a word store that answers “is this a word?” and “does any word start with this?”
signal: Words with the same start share one path of letters.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
twist: Trie search where “.” matches any letter at that spot.
prompt: Store words and search them, where a dot can stand for any one letter.
signal: Walk a tree of letters, and branch everywhere on a dot.

title: Word Search II
twist: Walk the board and the trie together, pruning dead letters.
prompt: Find every word from a list that can be traced through a board of letters.
signal: A tree of all the words lets you search them at once and drop dead paths.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Numbers arrive one at a time. Report the middle value at any moment.
signal: Keep the small half and big half apart, with each top on hand.

title: Combination Sum
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: List every way to pick numbers, repeats allowed, that add up to a target.
signal: Choose, go deeper, undo, try the next one.

title: Word Search
twist: Same try-and-undo walk, stepping to neighbour cells.
prompt: Can this word be traced through a letter grid without using a cell twice?
signal: Step to a neighbour, mark it, and unmark it on the way back.

title: Number of Islands
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Count the separate groups of land cells on a grid of land and water.
signal: Each new land cell starts a flood that claims its whole group.

title: Clone Graph
twist: Same flood, but copy each node as you claim it.
prompt: Make a full copy of a set of connected nodes, loops included.
signal: A map from old node to new node stops you copying anything twice.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
twist: Flood from both oceans, keep the overlap.
prompt: On a height map, find the cells where rain can drain to both the top-left and bottom-right seas.
signal: Work backwards: flood uphill from each sea and keep the overlap.

title: Course Schedule
twist: Flood along arrows; a loop means no schedule.
prompt: Some tasks must come before others. Can you finish them all?
signal: Tasks and rules form arrows. A loop makes it impossible.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
twist: Count the floods in a graph, not a grid.
prompt: Given nodes and links, count how many separate groups there are.
signal: Flood from each unvisited node, or join groups as you read the links.

title: Graph Valid Tree
twist: One flood plus no loops means a tree.
prompt: Do these links join all the nodes with no loops?
signal: Exactly n − 1 links, and one flood reaches everyone.

title: Climbing Stairs
twist: Warm-up: each step adds the two ways below it.
prompt: You climb one or two stairs at a time. How many ways can you reach the top?
signal: Ways to reach a stair: the ways to the two below it, added.

title: House Robber
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Pick values from a row, never two side by side, for the biggest total.
signal: At each spot: take it plus the best from two back, or skip it.

title: House Robber II
twist: Same street, but the ends are neighbours too.
prompt: Pick values from a circle, never two side by side, for the biggest total.
signal: Solve the row twice: once without the first item, once without the last.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
twist: Grow the answer out from each centre.
prompt: Find the longest stretch of a string that reads the same both ways.
signal: Expand from every centre: a long palindrome holds a shorter one.

title: Palindromic Substrings
twist: Count the palindromes around every centre.
prompt: Count how many stretches of a string read the same both ways.
signal: Every centre grows its own set of palindromes.

title: Decode Ways
twist: Each digit stands alone or pairs with its neighbour.
prompt: Digits stand for letters, 1 for A up to 26 for Z. How many ways can this digit string be read?
signal: Each position builds on the one-digit and two-digit reads before it.

title: Coin Change
twist: Fewest coins for each amount, built up amount by amount.
prompt: Find the fewest coins that add up to an amount.
signal: The best for an amount is one coin plus the best for what’s left.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
twist: Track the best and worst ending at each step.
prompt: Find the unbroken run of numbers with the largest product.
signal: A negative swaps best and worst, so track both.

title: Word Break
twist: Each cut asks whether the prefix already breaks.
prompt: Can this string be cut into words from a dictionary?
signal: A cut works if the part before it already works.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
twist: Each number extends the best run before it.
prompt: Find the longest chain of values that keeps rising, with gaps allowed.
signal: Each value extends the best chain ending at a smaller value.

title: Unique Paths
twist: Warm-up: each cell adds the ways from above and left.
prompt: A robot moves only right or down across a grid. How many routes reach the far corner?
signal: Ways into a cell: the ways from above plus the ways from the left.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Find the longest sequence of letters two strings share, in order, with gaps allowed.
signal: Two strings, two indices: fill a table of answers for every pair of prefixes.

title: Maximum Subarray
twist: Extend the running sum or restart it, keeping the best seen.
prompt: Find the unbroken run of numbers with the largest sum.
signal: If the running total goes negative, drop it and restart.

title: Jump Game
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Each number says how far you can hop. Can you get from the first spot to the last?
signal: Only the farthest reachable spot matters.

title: Insert Interval
twist: Slide the new interval into its sorted slot, then merge.
prompt: Add one new time range to a sorted list of ranges, joining any that touch.
signal: Copy what’s before, merge what overlaps, copy the rest.

title: Merge Intervals
twist: The one you just watched. Write it from memory.
prompt: Join every overlapping time range in a list.
signal: Sort by start. Each range either extends the last one or starts a new one.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
twist: Count the overlaps to remove instead of merging them.
prompt: Remove the fewest time ranges so the rest don’t overlap.
signal: Keep whichever ends first. It leaves the most room.

title: Meeting Rooms
twist: Warm-up: sort by start; any overlap means a clash.
prompt: Can one person attend every meeting on this list?
signal: Sort by start. Any overlap means a clash.

title: Meeting Rooms II
twist: Track how many meetings run at once; keep the peak.
prompt: How many rooms do you need to hold all these meetings?
signal: Sort starts and ends apart and track how many run at once.

title: Alien Dictionary
prompt: Work out a letter order from a sorted list of words in an unknown alphabet.
signal: Each neighbouring word pair gives one before-and-after rule. Order the rules with a topological sort.

title: Rotate Image
prompt: Turn a square grid 90 degrees clockwise, in place.
signal: Flip across the diagonal, then reverse each row.

title: Spiral Matrix
prompt: Read a grid in a spiral from the top-left corner inward.
signal: Track four walls and pull each one in after you walk it.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
prompt: If a cell is zero, set its whole row and column to zero, in place.
signal: Use the first row and column as your notepad.

title: Number of 1 Bits
prompt: Count the 1 bits in a number.
signal: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest 1 bit.

title: Counting Bits
prompt: For every number from 0 to n, count its 1 bits.
signal: bits(i) = bits(i >> 1) + (i & 1).

title: Reverse Bits
prompt: Flip the order of the 32 bits in a number.
signal: Shift bits off one end and onto the other.

title: Missing Number
prompt: One number from 0 to n is missing from an array. Find it.
signal: XOR everything, or compare against the expected sum.

title: Sum of Two Integers
prompt: Add two numbers without using + or −.
signal: XOR gives the sum without carries, AND gives the carries. Repeat.
